evidence: Read-only discovery on 2026-09-29 (scripts/signup-selectors.ts, session arm — windowed Chrome) and a page check the same day confirming an account signup, not a mailing list: myaccount.nytimes.com/auth/login, which redirects to /auth/enter-email, headed 'Log in or create an account'. Nothing was typed or submitted. 2026-10-01: real signup through the Agent Vault proxy using this recipe (vault-minted password), with browser egress through the owner's tunnel on a US network. Read with the staging network log (#734).
gotchas: One page for both signing in and signing up: it asks for the email first and decides from it. What a NEW address is shown next (a password to set, or a code sent by email) was not observed — look at the next screen before filling it. A code sent by email or text belongs to the account owner: hand it off.
A New York Times account is free; reading beyond the free allowance is a paid subscription, which is not part of this signup.
For a new address the step after the email is a create-account page with a single #password box and the same submit button; a known address gets a returning-user password step instead.

The test inbox's domain (agentmail.to) is refused at the create-account step: the request is answered 400 and the page shows 'Please enter a valid email address.', even though the email step accepted it. Use an address on a domain the site accepts.
